'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)|Israel–Hezbollah conflict]]
**[[September 2024 Lebanon strikes]]
***[[Hezbollah]] launches a [[ballistic missile]] targeting the [[Mossad]] [[headquarters]] in [[Tel Aviv]], [[Israel]], which is [[Iron Dome|intercepted]], while Israel conducts an additional 260 [[airstrike]]s across [[Lebanon]], killing at least 72 people. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/israel-prepares-potential-ground-invasion-lebanon-continues-airstrikes/story?id=114076028 (ABC News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/9/26/israel-attacks-lebanon-live-72-killed-in-latest-wave-of-israeli-attacks (Al Jazeera)]
**The [[United States]], the [[European Union]], and several other countries call for an immediate 21-day [[ceasefire]] along the [[Blue Line (withdrawal line)|Blue Line]] on the Israel–Lebanon border, which has been rejected by [[Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/lebanons-hezbollah-says-it-launched-rocket-targeting-mossad-base-near-tel-aviv-2024-09-25/ (Reuters)]
*[[Sectarian violence in Pakistan]], [[Shia–Sunni relations]]
**At least 25 people are killed and dozens are injured in clashes between [[Shia Islam|Shia]] and [[Sunni Islam|Sunni]] [[Islam in Pakistan|Muslim]] tribes in [[Kurram District]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]], since September 20. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-tribal-clashes-shiites-sunni-muslims-northwest-ce4a112ff34582e206861639e35132a2 (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Pakistani economic crisis (2022–present)|Pakistani economic crisis]]
**The [[International Monetary Fund]] approves a $7 billion loan for Pakistan to help its [[economy of Pakistan|economy]], with $1 billion being disbursed immediately and the rest in instalments over 37 months. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-imf-new-loan-board-of-executive-approved-3133c62867d5d60ec033e721daf7fead (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2024 Argentina wildfires]]
**Intense and widespread [[wildfire]]s in [[Córdoba Province, Argentina|Córdoba Province]], [[Argentina]], destroy {{conv|40000|ha|sqkm}} of forests and farmland, including several farm structures, and also kill large numbers of [[cattle]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/cattle-burn-monster-wildfires-rage-argentina-ranchlands-2024-09-25/ (Reuters)]
*A [[blimp]] promoting [[Brazil]] [[Association football|soccer team]] [[São Paulo FC]] crashes into houses in the Brazilian [[municipality]] of [[Osasco]], injuring the pilot. [https://www.foxnews.com/sports/blimp-promoting-brazilian-soccer-team-crashes-neighborhood-before-tournament-match (Fox News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Brazil–Ukraine relations]], [[China–Ukraine relations]]
**[[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian President]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] accuses Brazil and [[China]] of using their proposed peace plan for ending the [[Russo-Ukrainian War]] to increase their [[Geopolitics|geopolitical]] power "at [[Ukraine]]'s expense" by urging [[Developing country|developing nations]] to agree to the peace plan. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/zelenskiy-takes-aim-china-brazil-push-peace-ukraine-2024-09-25/ (Reuters)]
*[[Georgia–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] withdraws [[Prime Minister of Georgia|Georgian Prime Minister]] [[Irakli Kobakhidze]]'s invitation to attend a summit of national leaders hosted by [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] during the ongoing [[United Nations General Assembly]] session, and refuses any further delegator meetings with [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]], due to the "anti-democratic actions, disinformation, and negative rhetoric towards the U.S. and [[Western world|the West]]" resulting from Georgia's recently-passed [[2023–2024 Georgian protests|foreign agents law]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/georgian-pm-disinvited-biden-un-reception-relations-sour-2024-09-25/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Crime in France]], [[Immigration to France]]
**The [[Centre-right politics|center-right]] [[Emmanuel Macron|Macron]]-appointed [[Barnier government]] expresses a willingness to work with the [[Far-right politics|far-right]] [[National Rally]]'s proposals to strengthen [[France|French]] [[immigration to France|immigration]] and crime laws following the murder of a 19-year-old woman in [[Paris]] last week. The suspect, who was arrested in [[Geneva]], [[Switzerland]], is a [[Moroccans in France|Moroccan]] [[criminal conviction|convicted]] [[rape in France|rapist]] who was released from prison this month and was meant to be [[deport]]ed. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/after-student-murder-frances-rn-presses-government-be-tougher-security-2024-09-25/ (Reuters)]
*[[Criminal investigations into the Eric Adams administration]]
**[[Mayor of New York City|New York Mayor]] [[Eric Adams]] is indicted on federal charges following a [[Corruption in the United States|corruption]] investigation, becoming the first mayor of [[New York City]], United States, to face criminal charges while in office. [https://www.nytimes.com/live/2024/09/25/nyregion/eric-adams-indicted-corruption (''The New York Times'')]
*Four people are killed and two others are critically injured in a [[Spree killer|shooting spree]] in [[Nuoro]], [[Sardinia]], [[Italy]]. The perpetrator later [[murder-suicide|commits suicide]]. [https://www.ansa.it/sardegna/notizie/2024/09/25/strage-in-famiglia-a-nuoro-4-morti-e-3-feriti_3048baf4-f5eb-4df1-91f7-ac7d2c9fc1f0.html (ANSA)]
*A man [[carjacking|hijacks]] a [[Los Angeles Metro Bus]] in [[South Los Angeles]], [[California]], United States, later killing one of the two passengers. The bus is driven at gunpoint for more than {{conv|7|mi|km}} before the man surrenders to police. [https://apnews.com/article/los-angeles-metro-bus-hijacked-one-killed-c9b3a02f12c331ff228e3ce80a57c207 (AP)]
*Six people are injured when a bomb explodes in a courthouse in [[Santa Maria, California|Santa Maria]], California, United States. A suspect is later arrested. [https://www.cnn.com/2024/09/25/us/five-hurt-in-explosion-at-california-courthouse/index.html (CNN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 United States presidential election]], [[United States and the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|Speaker of the House]] [[Mike Johnson]] demands that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy [[dismissal (employment)|dismiss]] [[Ukrainian ambassador to the United States]] [[Oksana Markarova]] after Zelenskyy visited an ammunition factory in [[Pennsylvania]] with several [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] politicians, which Johnson claims represented [[Foreign electoral intervention|foreign electoral intervention]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/top-us-republican-wants-ukrainian-ambassador-fired-over-zelenskiy-factory-visit-2024-09-25/ (Reuters)]
*[[Cross-strait relations]]
**The [[Japan]]ese [[Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force|Navy]] sends a [[JS Sazanami|warship]] into the [[Taiwan Strait]] for the first time to reportedly "convey a message" to [[China]], according to Japanese newspaper ''[[Yomiuri Shimbun]]''. [https://www.dw.com/en/japan-sends-warship-into-taiwan-strait-for-first-time/a-70326923 (DW)]
*[[Alliance 90/The Greens|German Green Party]] leaders [[Omid Nouripour]] and [[Ricarda Lang]] state that they will step down following significant defeats in recent elections including the [[2024 Brandenburg state election]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/sep/25/leaders-germany-greens-party-resign-state-elections-ricarda-lang-omid-nouripour (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Government of Canada|Canadian]] [[Prime Minister of Canada|Prime Minister]] [[Justin Trudeau]] survives a [[no-confidence vote]] by a vote of 211–119. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c93pg0gnkvxo (BBC News)]
